title: Harness selection and execution — Grove caller views
intro: Target adoption design, pending implementation and acceptance: Ravel's corrected directory contract is integrated at b93bb927. The user supplies skills natively or through directory injection, subject to actual read access. Grove names a skill and the agent finds it. Process/result behavior remains as specified. Graphs begin at Start here, sequences at the first message, and states at the initial state.

groups.title: User-managed skill delivery
groups.description: User choice of delivery, subject to actual read access; no named-skill resolver in Grove or Ravel.

groups.title: Independent ownership
groups.description: Grove and Ravel meet at a public CLI. Grove launches ravel as an ordinary child, and Ravel keeps its own runner and release.

groups.title: Public process behavior
groups.description: Ravel routes and supervises, then returns an opaque argument after cleanup. Its own spec owns private runtime mechanics.

groups.title: Grove interpretation
groups.description: Grove owns launch admission, instructions, teardown and the meanings of grove-continue and grove-force-stop.

groups.title: Caller-owned creator evidence
groups.description: Grove policy assets and committed task receipts supply review evidence. Ravel supplies no store or run identity.

diagrams.title: User-managed skill delivery
diagrams.caption: The user may choose either route or retain both. Confined native access needs separate proof; installation under HOME grants no reads. Directory readability proves neither skill presence nor adherence. Missing mandated guidance ends with force-stop.

diagrams.title: Preserving readers through adoption
diagrams.caption: Target design, not completed rollout. Every intermediate tap dependency remains compatible. Cleanup is optional and manual. Existing session ending commands remain valid; old callers retain compatible prefixes and settings.

diagrams.title: Independent caller and process-manager boundary
diagrams.caption: Separate prefixes and versions, ordinary caller imports, Grove's shared job function and Ravel's own runner. No shared Rust library or bundled Ravel worker. Ravel alone gives the cleanup assurance.

diagrams.title: Route, supervise and return an argument
diagrams.caption: Optional directory injection precedes selection. The agent finds the named skill using the user-selected route. Refusal launches nothing; successful cleanup returns only the opaque result.

diagrams.title: Two nested jobs and terminal ownership
diagrams.caption: Grove launches ravel as its foreground job and sends a caught TERM or HUP to ravel alone. Ravel manages the harness job and its cleanup. Each supervisor takes the terminal back from its own child. Descendants that escape a group are outside its cleanup guarantee.

diagrams.title: Observable session result lifecycle
diagrams.caption: A reading aid for public behavior, not a checked model or a description of private transport. A published result can succeed despite the managed process later exiting nonzero.

diagrams.title: Lifecycle and confined standalone callers
diagrams.caption: Both callers use one shared job function and may receive directory hints. Exact caller ending commands remain intact. Lifecycle and standalone result meanings stay unchanged.

diagrams.title: Grove post-reap decision order
diagrams.caption: Epoch invalidation gates interpretation. A failed spawn or wait reads no disposition. After any error, Grove reports it and dies of a caught signal. Driver interruption precedes successful exact force-stop, then teardown, then successful exact continuation. Grove checks no process group after the reap. Force-stop exits 1 without undoing teardown.

diagrams.title: Creator evidence and rejected alternatives
diagrams.caption: Inline selected receipts or explicit owner declarations avoid a store namespace and preserve finishing-attempt origin. They are same-user attestations.

diagrams.title: Finishing producer pins evidence for review
diagrams.caption: Grove caller assets wrap selection and read committed task evidence. Retirement renames only; the finishing session writes Creator lines and commits them.

diagrams.title: Configured review selection from caller evidence
diagrams.caption: The configured-review branch of Grove's opt-in policy. Nonreview routing is outside this view. Missing/invalid/legacy evidence or a same-provider route refuses.

discussion.title: Grove names skills; the user supplies them
discussion.status: Integrated directory contract; adoption implementation and acceptance pending
discussion.summary: Ravel's corrected contract is integrated at b93bb927. Native installation and directory injection remain user choices with distinct access obligations. Adoption adds missing-skill force-stop, namespace-neutral requests and compatible intermediate tap states.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Clarified confined native access and missing-skill force-stop, with discovery owned by the agent.
Recorded the integrated upstream contract, compatible tap ordering and manual cleanup.
Added optional directory injection and preserved caller bytes.
Placed directory hints before owner policy evaluation.
Applied optional directory delivery to both callers.
